section_title: What keeps the sanctuary’s portion set apart?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 8 Bordering the territory of Judah, from east to west, will be the portion you are to set apart. It will be 25,000 cubits wide, and the length of a tribal portion from east to west. In the center will be the sanctuary. 9 The special portion you set apart to the LORD shall be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. 10 This will be the holy portion for the priests. It will be 25,000 cubits long on the north side, 10,000 cubits wide on the west side, 10,000 cubits wide on the east side, and 25,000 cubits long on the south side. In the center will be the sanctuary of the LORD. 11 It will be for the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray. 12 It will be a special portion for them set apart from the land, a most holy portion adjacent to the territory of the Levites.

13 Bordering the territory of the priests, the Levites shall have an area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The whole length will be 25,000 cubits, and the width 10,000 cubits. 14 They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land, for it is holy to the LORD.

context_lines: Next to Judah is the district set apart for the Lord, with the sanctuary at its center. A holy portion is assigned to the priests from Zadok’s family, who kept the Lord’s charge.
The Levites have their portion beside the priests. The land set apart for this service may not be sold, exchanged or transferred away, because it is holy to the Lord.

The arrangement carries forward the distinction between the priests and the other Levites described in chapter 44. It also protects the land assigned to worship and service from being treated as ordinary property for sale.
common_interpretation_lines: [Cambridge](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/ezekiel/48.htm) explains this section as the priests’ domain and the adjoining Levitical provision. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/48.htm) places the assigned portions within the wider picture of restored life before God.
The purpose of setting the land apart is stated directly: it belongs to the Lord’s holy provision. No additional meaning has to be assigned to every dimension to recognize that purpose.
